title: Finite continuous ordered-coset chain projection
statement:
Let $G$ be a topological group, let $H\subseteq G$ be an open subgroup of finite index, let $n\geq1$, and choose $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in G$. Let $B_q(G)$ be the free abelian group with basis $[x_0,\ldots,x_q]$ for all tuples in $G^{q+1}$, repetitions allowed, and $B_{-1}(G)=\mathbf Z[\varnothing]$, with alternating-deletion boundary $\partial$, augmentation $\partial[x]=[\varnothing]$, and $\partial[\varnothing]=0$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $J_q$ be the free abelian group on symbols $[(i_0,z_0),\ldots,(i_q,z_q)]$ with $0\leq i_0<\cdots<i_q\leq n$ and $z_j\in Ha_{i_j}$, with the same boundary and augmentation; $J_{-1}=\mathbf Z[\varnothing]$. Write $e_q:J_q\to B_q(G)$ for erasure of colors. For $h\in H$ let $S^h$ be the specified ordered-join operator of [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction], with chosen vertices $ha_i$.
There is a finite transversal $D$ of the right cosets $H\backslash G$ containing $1$. The unique factorization $x=\rho(x)s(x)$ with $\rho(x)\in H$, $s(x)\in D$ defines a continuous map $\rho:G\to H$ satisfying $\rho(hx)=h\rho(x)$ for $h\in H$. For any such transversal define homomorphisms $P_q:B_q(G)\to J_q$ by linear extension of
$$P_{-1}=1,\qquad P_0[x]=[(0,\rho(x)a_0)],\qquad P_q[x_0,\ldots,x_q]=S^{\rho(x_0)}_{q-1}\bigl(P_{q-1}(\partial[x_0,\ldots,x_q])\bigr)\quad(1\leq q\leq n).$$
Then $\partial^2=0$ on both augmented chain groups, $e$ commutes with $\partial$, and $\partial P_q=P_{q-1}\partial$ for $0\leq q\leq n$. All $P_q$ and $A_q=e_qP_q$ are $H$-equivariant for coordinatewise left translation, and $A_{-1}=1$. For each $0\leq q\leq n$ the value $P_q[x]$ has an expansion as a fixed finite integer sum of colored symbols whose vertices have the form $\rho(x_j)a_i$. Its integer coefficients, color lists and selections of the input positions $j$ do not depend on $x$; repeated terms are retained. Consequently $A_q[x]$ is a fixed finite integer sum of basis tuples obtained from continuous maps $G^{q+1}\to G^{q+1}$. Every tuple in the expansion of $A_n[x]$ belongs to $Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n$. All choices and expansions are independent of coefficient spaces, and no normality of $H$ is required.

proof.text: Choose one representative of each of the finitely many right cosets $Hd$, choosing $1$ for $H$, and call the set $D$. For $x\in Hd$, put $s(x)=d$ and $\rho(x)=xd^{-1}\in H$. Distinct cosets are disjoint, and $x=hd$ forces $h=xd^{-1}$, proving uniqueness. Each $Hd$ is open: right multiplication by $d$ and its inverse are continuous by the topological-group axioms. On this open set $\rho$ is the continuous map $x\mapsto xd^{-1}$ into the subspace $H$; for open $U\subseteq H$, its inverse image is the union over $d\in D$ of these open inverse images in $Hd$, hence open in $G$. If $h\in H$, then $hx\in Hd$ whenever $x\in Hd$, so $\rho(hx)=hxd^{-1}=h\rho(x)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic auxiliary expansion: continuous right-coset retraction; not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: On tuple chains $B(G)$, deleting original positions $i<j$ in the two possible orders gives the same tuple with coefficients $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$, which cancel. This proves $\partial^2=0$, including degree one where the resulting tuple is empty; in degrees zero and $-1$ it is zero by definition. On $J$, square-zero is the assertion of [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction] with $r=n+1$ and $X_i=Ha_i$. Erasure commutes with boundary since both composites give the same alternating list of erased faces; at degree zero both give $[\varnothing]$. Erasure commutes with translation for the same coordinatewise reason.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic auxiliary expansion: boundaries and erasure; not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Define $T_q:B_q(G)\to B_q(H)$ on basis tuples by $T_q[x_0,\ldots,x_q]=[\rho(x_0),\ldots,\rho(x_q)]$ and $T_{-1}=1$, extending by finite integer sums using [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Applying $\rho$ before or after deleting a position gives identical tuples with identical signs, so $\partial T_q=T_{q-1}\partial$, also at augmentation. Step 1 gives $T_q(hx)=hT_q(x)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic auxiliary expansion: coordinatewise retraction of tuple chains; not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ordered-join-coset-comparison] to the underlying group $G$, its subgroup $H$, the given $n\geq1$ and the $a_i$. Write $\bar P_q:B_q(H)\to J_q$ for its maps. The present $P_q$ equals $\bar P_qT_q$: this is the displayed formula in degrees $-1,0$; assuming equality in degree $q-1$, the composite on $[x]$ is $S^{\rho(x_0)}_{q-1}\bar P_{q-1}(\partial T_q[x])=S^{\rho(x_0)}_{q-1}P_{q-1}(\partial[x])$, exactly the required recursion. Thus its homomorphisms are defined by that recursion. The cited chain and equivariance identities, composed with those for $T$, give $\partial P_q=P_{q-1}\partial$ and $H$-equivariance in every required degree. Step 2 gives the same for $A=eP$, and $A_{-1}=1$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic auxiliary expansion: assembly of the specified recursion with the existing subgroup-tuple comparison; not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Take the fixed finite lists in [lem-sfb-ordered-join-coset-comparison] and substitute $h_j=\rho(x_j)$ in its displayed expansion. Step 4 identifies the result with $P_q[x]$. The coefficients, colors and input indices are unchanged, including repeated terms. After erasure each coordinate is $\rho(x_j)a_i$, a continuous function of $x$ by step 1 and continuity of multiplication, hence each tuple map is continuous in the product topology. At degree $n$ each color list has $n+1$ distinct increasing entries in $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, hence is exactly $0,\ldots,n$; its $i$th erased coordinate lies in $Ha_i$. All constructions use only integer chains and the fixed group data, so they are independent of coefficient spaces. No step uses normality of $H$.

Read the full statements of def-weil-pbc-free-module, lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction (reviewed, Q136) and lem-sfb-ordered-join-coset-comparison (reviewed, Q157). Step 1 builds a finite right-coset transversal with 1 in it and ρ(x)=xd⁻¹ on each coset Hd. Each Hd is open because right translation is a homeomorphism, so ρ is continuous by gluing over a finite open cover, and ρ(hx)=hρ(x); normality of H is never used. Step 2 checks the sign pairing for ∂²=0 on B(G); on J, ∂²=0 is the contraction node's own clause with r=n+1 and X_i=Ha_i, and its J_q=0 for q≥r matches the item's empty J_q for q>n. Step 3 defines T as ρ applied to each coordinate; it commutes with ∂ and with the H-action. Step 4: I checked by induction that P_q=P̄_qT_q, with base case [(0,ρ(x_0)a_0)]. This gives ∂P_q=P_{q-1}∂ and H-equivariance for 0≤q≤n from the cited clauses; the comparison node's hypotheses (G, H, n≥1, any a_i) all hold. Step 5 substitutes h_j=ρ(x_j) into the comparison node's fixed-list expansion clause, so each tuple is a continuous function of x, and in top degree the colors are forced to be 0..n, which gives support in Ha_0×…×Ha_n. Small cases: for n=1, ∂P_1=P_0∂ by hand; H=G gives ρ=id; H={1} forces G finite discrete; coinciding cosets and non-normal H also work. proof_deps equal the union of the step uses.
